name: @go-gost/mcp

tools.name: gost-run
tools.description: Send one HTTP(S) request through an egress profile and return the status, headers, body, timings, and any classified failure. The egress is a configured profile name, never a URL, and the request cannot fall back to a direct connection. A non-2xx status is still a successful call; only a transport failure sets ok=false. Discover the profile names with the gost-mcp://egress resource.

egress.description: name of the configured egress profile to send the request through

url.description: absolute http or https URL to request

headers.description: literal request headers; no secret indirection

body.description: request body, interpreted according to body_encoding

timeout_ms.description: total request timeout in milliseconds; capped at 120000

max_bytes.description: response body read limit in bytes; capped at 8388608

follow_redirects.description: follow up to 5 redirects; defaults to true

tools.name: gost-trace
tools.description: Diagnose connectivity through an egress profile stage by stage: local resolve, connect, TLS, and HTTP/read or a DNS query. It traces cumulative chain prefixes (direct, hop 0, hop 0+1, ...), not per-hop TTL hops, and stops at the first failing prefix. It is not a traceroute: a gost chain is a sequence of proxy hops, and per-hop timing inside one hop is not observable. A timeout returns the prefixes that completed, with ok=false. Discover the profile names with the gost-mcp://egress resource.

egress.description: name of the configured egress profile to diagnose through

target.description: host:port, http(s) URL, udp://host:port, tls://host:port, or dns://name

mode.description: auto (default), tcp, udp, dns, tls, http, or https

resolver.description: DNS resolver host:port for mode=dns; defaults to the first nameserver in /etc/resolv.conf

prefix.description: probe cumulative chain prefixes (direct, hop 0, hop 0+1, ...); defaults to true

timeout_ms.description: budget for the whole trace in milliseconds; capped at 60000

payload.description: optional bytes to send, base64 encoded, for tcp and udp

expect.description: optional substring expected in the reply

identity.description: also fetch the public egress identity from the configured endpoint

tools.name: gost-unwisp
tools.description: Release a wisp lease early and close its tunnel. It is idempotent: an unknown, expired, or already released handle returns released=false instead of an error. Read gost-mcp://leases to find the current handles and URLs.

tools.name: gost-wisp
tools.description: Publish a loopback HTTP service at a public wisp URL for a bounded lease and return its handle. The URL is public and unauthenticated: anyone who learns it can reach the local service, so the local service must authenticate its own users. The target must resolve inside the configured gost-wisp.allow list (loopback by default), and ttl_s is capped by gost-wisp.max_ttl. Release it early with gost-unwisp; a relay may re-bind the tunnel, so read the current URL from the gost-mcp://leases resource. A publish failure is reported as ok=false with a failure object.

local.description: loopback target to publish as host:port, such as 127.0.0.1:3000; it must resolve inside the configured gost-wisp.allow list

ttl_s.description: lease lifetime in seconds; defaults to 900 and is capped by gost-wisp.max_ttl

label.description: free-text label for logs and the lease listing; never part of the public URL

verify.description: request the public URL once after publishing; defaults to true

instructions: gost-mcp is a network toolbox with four tools. Pass gost-run and gost-trace an egress profile name from the gost-mcp://egress resource; never put a proxy URI in the egress field. Use gost-trace to find the first failing stage (resolve, connect, tls, http) instead of guessing. gost-wisp publishes a loopback HTTP service at a public, unauthenticated URL: call it only when the user explicitly asks to expose a service, keep the TTL short, and release it with gost-unwisp. A non-2xx HTTP status from gost-run is a normal result, not a failed tool call.
